extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners, Interference Practice Specialists (IPS), and patent practitioners involved in interference proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on identifying, suggesting, handling, and resolving patent interference proceedings (priority contests) under 35 U.S.C. 135 and related regulations, intended principally for patent examiners and IPSes. Covers searches, file control, counts/claim correspondence, threshold issues, actions during and after interferences, estoppel, and related procedural requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory basis for interferences
rubrics_metrics.description: An interference is a contest under 35 U.S.C. 135(a) between an application and either another application or a patent to determine priority within the meaning of 35 U.S.C. 102(g)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See cited statutes (35 U.S.C. 102, 104, 135) for consequences (e.g., cancellation, issuance to prior inventor) and limitations (e.g., expired patents cannot be in interference).

rubrics_metrics.name: Interfering subject matter (37 CFR 41.203)
rubrics_metrics.description: An interference exists if the subject matter of a claim of one party would, if prior art, have anticipated or rendered obvious the subject matter of a claim of the opposing party and vice versa; 'same invention' means patentably indistinct inventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply familiar anticipation/obviousness principles; identical claim language does not guarantee same invention—construe claims in light of their own specifications. See multiple examples (Markush groups, genus/species, means-plus-function) illustrating how interference-in-fact is determined.

rubrics_metrics.name: Count definition and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: A count is the Board’s description of the interfering subject matter that sets the scope of admissible proofs on priority; where there is more than one count, each count must describe a patentably distinct invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Every count must have at least one corresponding claim for each party; counts define what proofs are admissible on priority issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim correspondence test (37 CFR 41.207(b)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: To determine whether a claim corresponds to a count, assume the subject matter of the count is prior art to the party; if the count would have anticipated or rendered the claim obvious, the claim corresponds to the count.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At least one corresponding claim required per party; a claim may correspond to multiple counts. Examples clarify genus/species and Markush situations where anticipation vs obviousness matters and may require showing of prior art to support obviousness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Broadest reasonable construction (37 CFR 41.200(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: A claim shall be given its broadest reasonable construction in light of the specification of the application or patent in which it appears for interference purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpret claim terms in context of the particular specification; means-plus-function limitations may produce different scopes depending on corresponding structure disclosed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completion of examination before initiating contested case (37 CFR 41.102)
rubrics_metrics.description: Before a contested case is initiated, examination or reexamination must be completed, and there must be at least one claim that is patentable but for a judgment in the contested case and would be involved in the contested case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All pending claims must be allowed, finally rejected, or canceled; any appeals or petitions must be decided. Use form paragraph 23.01 to notify applicants when a request for interference is premature because examination is incomplete.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interference search requirements (2304.01(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: When an application is in condition for allowance, an interference search must be made by performing a text search of the 'US-PGPUB' database in EAST or WEST directed to the comprehensive inventive features in the broadest claim; sequence claims require STIC sequence search requests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A printout of the databases searched, the queries used, and the date must be made of record in the application file; the search results must not be placed in the application file. If potential interfering subject matter is identified, review and follow Chapter 2300 guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search scope not limited to original classification
rubrics_metrics.description: The search for interfering applications must not be limited to the class or subclass in which the application is classified but must be extended to all classes, including those outside the Technology Center, where necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP §1302.08 for cross-class searching; interference searches should be comprehensive across relevant fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consult an Interference Practice Specialist (IPS)
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners must consult immediately with an IPS in the examiner’s Technology Center when a possible interference is identified; an IPS must approve any referral of a suggested interference to the Board and sign the completed Form PTO-850 or the TC Director may sign.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IPSes keep current via consultation with APJs, handle referrals, and may arrange APJ consultation as needed; examiners should promptly address IPS inquiries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obtaining control over involved files / assignment
rubrics_metrics.description: Ordinarily, applications believed to interfere should be assigned to the same examiner. If applications are in different Technology Centers, reassign so both are in the TC where the commonly claimed invention would be classified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After termination of interference, further transfer may be appropriate depending on outcome.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of non-converted paper file wrappers and benefit files
rubrics_metrics.description: All files, including older paper benefit application files and any artifacts not converted to Image File Wrapper (IFW), must be available to the examiner before referring a suggested interference; lost paper file wrappers must be reconstructed prior to referral.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete patent and benefit files are necessary for determining whether benefit should be accorded for 35 U.S.C. 102(g)(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction practice for interfering vs non-interfering claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Restriction of interfering claims from non-interfering claims, or from unpatentable claims whose further prosecution would unduly delay initiation of the interference, can be appropriate under 35 U.S.C. 121; consult IPS when imposing such restrictions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants may instead cancel claims and refile in continuation applications; issuing non-interfering claims promptly is important to avoid unjustified delay given patent term adjustments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practices on issuance vs suspension (Practices 2–5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Generally issue allowed applications rather than suspend. If two applications claim same invention and one is in condition for allowance while the other is not, issue the allowable one (Practice 2). If both are in condition and earliest effective filing dates within six months, an A v A interference may be suggested (Practice 3). If not within six months, the earlier-filed should be issued (Practice 4). Suspension is discouraged (Practice 5).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If both ready to issue and dates within six months, suggestion possible; but do not use suspension to create ties or to delay issuance unnecessarily; consider 37 CFR 41.202(d) showings where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written description and late-claiming bars as threshold scrutiny
rubrics_metrics.description: Enforcement of the written description requirement under 35 U.S.C. 112, first paragraph, and the late claiming bars under 35 U.S.C. 135(b) are closely scrutinized before declaring an interference and are treated as threshold issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These issues preserve integrity and efficiency of interference practice; consult 37 CFR 41.201 'Threshold issue' definition and IPS as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Threshold issues (37 CFR 41.201)
rubrics_metrics.description: Threshold issue means an issue that, if resolved in favor of the movant, would deprive the opponent of standing in the interference; may include no interference-in-fact, repose under 35 U.S.C. 135(b), or unpatentability for lack of written description under 35 U.S.C. 112(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Threshold issues should be identified early; their resolution can preclude initiation of interference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resolve outstanding patent matters before suggesting interference
rubrics_metrics.description: Patents undergoing reexamination, reissue, petitions for late maintenance fees, disclaimers, corrections, or inventorship corrections must have such issues resolved before an interference is suggested because they may affect whether or how an interference may be declared.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: an expired patent (maintenance fee not timely paid) cannot be in interference until petition to accept delayed payment is granted; inventorship correction that makes inventors identical eliminates basis for interference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secrecy order handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Secrecy order cases (e.g., one application under secrecy order) require special handling; patentability of claims in non-secrecy applications should be processed (e.g., allow and issue) where appropriate despite secrecy in others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult IPS and applicable statutes/regulations; example given where a transistor claim should be allowed even though another related application is under secrecy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jurisdiction of the Board during interference (37 CFR 41.103)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board acquires jurisdiction over any involved file when it initiates a contested case; other proceedings for the involved file within the Office are suspended except as the Board may order; the examiner generally may not act on an involved patent or application without Board authorization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Board may consult the examiner on technical matters; termination defined as final Board judgment and expiration/completion of judicial review per 37 CFR 41.205(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on ex parte communications (37 CFR 41.11)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ex parte communications about a contested case or inter partes reexamination with a Board member or employee assigned to the proceeding are not permitted; any attempt by a party to communicate with the Board through the examiner or to have the examiner act in an involved file without Board authorization should be reported.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Improper communications may lead to Board sanctions or referral to the Office of Enrollment and Discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to related files (37 CFR 41.109)
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests for access to or copies of Office records directly related to a contested case must be filed with the Board and precisely identify the records; ordinarily authorized records include the application file for an involved patent, an involved application, and any application for which benefit has been accorded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Opposing parties may be authorized access under 37 CFR 41.109 in addition to public access under 37 CFR 1.11/1.14; filing fees apply for copies under §1.19(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension of related examinations
rubrics_metrics.description: Examination may continue in related cases, including benefit files; once related file examination is completed, consult IPS to determine further action. Suspension may be necessary if claims would be barred by a loss in the interference, but steps should be taken to minimize patent term adjustment effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider restriction of application to non-interfering claims so they can be issued and divert interfering claims to a divisional that can be suspended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adding additional parties to an interference
rubrics_metrics.description: If during prosecution the examiner discovers other applications or patents claiming the same invention but not currently involved in the interference, the examiner should consult with an IPS and prepare a referral to the Board to suggest addition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additions follow same referral preparation process as the original suggestion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board orders affecting related files
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board may order a paper to be filed in a related application to notify the examiner of facts (e.g., party admission, prior art) relevant to examination of the related case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners should act on such Board-ordered filings as directed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of judgment within the Office (37 CFR 41.127)
rubrics_metrics.description: A Board judgment disposes of all issues that were or could have been properly raised and decided; adverse judgment constitutes final refusal/cancellation; judgment may include a recommendation for further action by the examiner or Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner must enter and maintain recommended rejections unless an applicant files an amendment or shows facts not previously of record that overcome the recommended rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final disposal of claims after interference
rubrics_metrics.description: Judgment against a claim in an interference finally disposes of the claim; no further action is needed by the examiner on that claim. If no claim remains allowable to the applicant, issue a notice of abandonment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If judgment contains no recommendation, examiner should update the search and may reopen prosecution for unresolved claims at discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Added or amended claims during interference
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant may file a motion during the interference to add or amend a claim; a patentee may file a reissue application in support of such a motion. The paper adding/amending will be placed in the official record but not entered unless and to the extent authorized by the Board.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner may only enter added/amended claims if authorized by the Board, and can still reject those claims during further prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Estoppel within the Office (two types)
rubrics_metrics.description: Losing-party estoppel: (1) merits estoppel — losing party is barred on the merits from seeking claims that would have been anticipated/rendered obvious by the lost count; (2) procedural estoppel — losing party is barred from seeking Office relief that could have been sought during the interference but was not.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Estoppel may apply to generic claims encompassing lost subject matter and to later-filed continuation claims; examiner should consult an IPS before allowing a claim to a losing party that was added/amended post-interference. Examples are provided showing applications of both estoppel types.

rubrics_metrics.name: No interference-in-fact and its consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: A judgment of no interference-in-fact means no interference is needed to resolve priority between the parties; neither party has lost for the purpose of estoppel, and no second interference should occur between the same parties on patentably indistinct subject matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an applicant was prevented by the Board from seeking relief during the interference, procedural estoppel may not apply; a no-interference-in-fact judgment bars any further interference between same parties on the same invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: No second interference policy
rubrics_metrics.description: No second interference should occur between the same parties on patentably indistinct subject matter; a prior Board holding of no interference-in-fact may not be reopened in further examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a party that lost the earlier interference again claims the same invention as the count, interfering claims should be rejected as estopped.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special ownership contests (NASA/DoE)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board determines ownership contests arising from inventions made pursuant to government contracts under statutes for NASA (42 U.S.C. 2457) and DoE (42 U.S.C. 2182); interference practices generally apply to these contests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must file statements regarding making/conception and relation to government contracts; coordinate with Licensing and Review and IPS when suggesting such cases to the Board.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions relevant to interference practice (37 CFR 41.2/41.201)
rubrics_metrics.description: Key defined terms include affidavit, Board, involved claim (claim designated as corresponding to the count), involved (Board declared subject of contested case), constructive reduction to practice, earliest constructive reduction to practice, senior/junior party, threshold issue, business day, and others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Earliest constructive reduction to practice requires continuous disclosure through a chain of applications (35 U.S.C. 120/121 or timely 119/365 filings). Senior party entitled to presumption under §41.207(a)(1).
